result.what_works:
Hope and discontent are a REASON LEDGER, not two floats. Nothing moves a meter without going through `SocietyLedger.add(meter, key, label, text, delta, rate, tick)`, and every reason carries a sentence built from this run's numbers ("Eleven of nineteen homes are below twelve degrees. The coldest is at -9."), a live rate per in-world hour, and what it has cost today and across the whole run. A test asserts the reasons sum EXACTLY to the bar, including when a meter is pinned at 0 or 100 (contributions are scaled by the fraction of movement that actually happened). A reason that stops acting has its rate zeroed but keeps its history, so a tooltip never reports a problem the player already solved.

HOPE HAS AN EARNED CEILING. Comfort (warm/fed/housed/well + solace) sets a ceiling of 26..92; standing positive forces fade out as hope approaches it, and above it hope decays back down. Only things that HAPPEN (a night survived, a wave held, a promise kept, research finished, a law signed) push past it. This was a real fix: before it, the reference run ended at hope 96 / discontent 0, i.e. comfort bought unlimited hope and the meter stopped being a question.

THE BOOK OF LAWS: 31 authored pages (`game/content/laws/*.tres`, single prose source at `game/content/laws/_write_the_book.py`) across a shared Necessity trunk plus mutually exclusive Order and Faith branches. Each has prose, a case for, a case against, and a line for the morning after. Prerequisites gate; exclusions are declared once and made symmetric AND TRANSITIVE by LawBook, so signing The Pits shuts Named Graves, Snow Burial and The Rite of Ash, and committing to The Watch greys out the entire Faith branch with a worded reason per page. Scarcity: one law argued at a time, per-law debate hours, then an 18-hour seal.

LAWS ARE NOT PANEL NUMBERS. [P05] citizens exposes `set_shift_law` / `set_child_labour` / `set_elder_labour` ("society enacts, we obey"); society pushes work_hours -> standard/extended/emergency and the child/elder flags straight into it, and two world tests prove the wire is live end to end (sign Emergency Shift -> citizens reports `extended` with its real fatigue/output/morale coefficients).

SIX OVERLAPPING FACTIONS form grievances with hysteresis (1.5h sustained to open, 1h + decayed intensity to close), which cost discontent proportional to how many people hold them, then escalate into DEMANDS with deadlines and machine-checkable terms in three shapes: reach a metric, sign one of these laws, or sign NONE of these laws before the deadline. Meeting one buys approval and takes anger off the bar; missing one radicalises the faction permanently (shorter fuses, sharper penalties).

THREE ENDINGS, ALL TELEGRAPHED: exile at max discontent, despair at zero hope, extinction at zero population. Each of the first two has a four-rung worded ladder and then a survivable 12-hour countdown that lifts if the meter recovers. The ladder advances at most one rung per sample, so no single catastrophic impulse can skip the warnings (covered by a test that shoves discontent 0 -> 100 in one tick and asserts all three warnings still fire first).

Verified in a real long run: `economy_60min` (72000 ticks) opens grievances, issues 13 demands, fails 12, radicalises four factions to approval -95, climbs through all four unrest rungs and ends `exiled` at tick 26980.

REPO-WIDE DETERMINISM TRAP I hit and worked around only inside my own folder: Array.sort() on StringName does NOT sort alphabetically. StringName's comparison operator compares the interned pointer, so [&"zebra", &"alpha", &"middle"].sort() returns [&"zebra", &"middle", &"alpha"] (verified empirically in this build). It is stable within one process only while interning order is stable, which is why it survives tools/determinism.sh (two fresh processes intern in the same order) and then diverges the moment one process builds the same set twice in a different order — exactly how two identical seeded society runs produced different serialize() output. game/core/registry.gd `ids()` and `all()` do this and their doc comment claims 'sorted by id so iteration is deterministic'; there are ~116 further .sort() calls across game/sim outside society/. Someone who owns core should audit these. Dictionary[String, ...] keys are fine; only StringName is affected.

That was the round 1 critique and I have not fixed it, I have only made it possible to fix: every number a HUD needs is exposed and worded (hope_reasons with per-reason rate/today/total/sentence, hope_ceiling as a mark on the bar, book_view with a human reason per blocked page, demands with terms and hours_left, warning_state with the countdown). It is fully exercised in artifacts/p06_econ (economy_60min, 72000 ticks): grievances open, 13 demands issued, 12 failed, four factions radicalised to approval -95, all four unrest rungs fired, run ends `exiled` at tick 26980. **The balance table** (`game/sim/economy/`, `game/content/economy/`). `BalanceTable` holds material prices, starting stock, deposit yields, the heat planning budget, population growth/death, research and defence envelopes, global difficulty knobs, and the audit bands. `DifficultyCurve` states the intended experience of days 1–7 as measurable bands. **It does not copy content it does not own.** `Balance.audit()` measures [P11]'s 24 building definitions against design bands, scoped by what a building is *for* (a smelter that vents 4 heat while drawing 14 is a consumer; an accumulator is a tank; a watchtower drawing 1.0 is neither; turrets are explicitly not audited on heat because that band belongs to [P07]). `audit_research()` prices [P10]'s 45-node tree and checks per-tier progression (measured: 153 → 574 → 1158 → 3020 points/unlock). `audit_threat()` reads [P08]'s live `ThreatProfile` and checks its curve against what a city following the intended build order can arm. A real population, not a counter. `game/sim/citizens/` (5 files, 3.6k lines) + `tests/citizens/` (2 suites, 791 lines).

**Individuals stored as columns.** `CitizenPool` is structure-of-arrays: ~30 packed arrays indexed by slot, slots recycled smallest-first, `alive` kept as a sorted slot list. Every citizen has a first/last name from a 48x42 table, an age that advances, an age bracket (child/adult/elder), one of six traits that change how fast they get cold, sick, tired and bitter, health/warmth/hunger/fatigue/morale/illness/injury, a job, a home, a shift and an 8-state machine (idle, walking, working, sleeping, eating, sick, injured, dead).

**Needs wired to the rest of the sim for real.** Warmth converges on the felt temperature at the citizen's own tile: `ClimateSystem.ambient_temperature()` + `HeatSystem.warmth_field().value_at(cell)` + a roof, where the roof's value is `SHELTER_C x insulation x served`, and `served` is [P02]'s per-building delivered fraction. A browned-out district is therefore literally a district where people get cold, fall ill, stop working, and stop making heat. Hunger is drawn as whole `ration`/`grain` units from `BuildSystem.stock` (the same BuildStock façade production uses) with a founders' larder behind it; under a day of food left the city goes to half rations. Rest is gated by housing (a bed is -0.85 fatigue/s, sleeping rough is -0.22) and by shift law.

**Jobs and staffing.** `CitizenJobBoard` mirrors [P11]'s buildings into sorted records, derives trade/infirmary/kitchen/hazard roles from tags and category (no building is named in code), finds each building a walkable door, hires the nearest idle adult in `build_priority` order, and writes the crew size back into `BuildingInstance.workers`. `staffing_of(id)` reports who is actually STANDING there, not who is on the roster, so a shift change visibly starves output. `idle_builders()` feeds `BuildSystem.build_power()`.

**Day rhythm.** Shifts read `ClimateSystem.phase_of_day`; three laws (standard/extended/emergency) are phase bitmasks with fatigue, output and morale costs. In first_night the city measurably fills and empties: working 0→15, walking 0→22, asleep 0→30 over one day.

**Walking.** [P01]'s A* via `GridSystem.find_path`, deduplicated by (door, door) so a whole shift shares one search, budgeted to one search per tick, node-capped quadratically (the grid's octile heuristic is under-weighted ~6:1 against its terrain-cost g, so the search behaves like Dijkstra), and invalidated per-cell when the city builds on a path rather than by wiping the cache. 1018 citizens over 1000 ticks: 181 searches, 1375 cache hits.

**Death with a cause.** Six causes, chosen by what was actually killing them. Each death emits `Bus.citizen_died(id, cause)` plus a severity-1 worded alert ("Ewa Kowal, 68, pensioner, died of old age."), goes into a 48-deep obituary with age/trade/cell/homeless/employed for [P22], and knocks city-wide morale via a decaying grief term.

**Legibility (the round-1 gap).** `citizen_info(id)` returns 34 fields including a ready-to-print `summary`: "Emrik Steen, 53, tinsmith — holding up, working at Smelter". Every citizen serialises that string into state.json. `agents_for_view()` implements the renderer's existing agent contract (ids offset by 5,000,000 so they cannot collide with [P07]'s enemies) — citizens are on screen with no work from [P13]. `citizen_at_cell` / `citizens_in_cell_rect` give click-to-inspect; `citizen_overlay_rows()` gives [P19] per-person warmth/morale/health; `report()` gives [P17] the whole city in one dictionary.

known_gaps: Walking uses [P01]'s A* (GridSystem.find_path) with a shared route cache, NOT the flow field the brief named. A flow field converges on one goal set and citizens have hundreds of distinct doors; the flow field is still the right tool for [P08]'s waves. The cost of that choice is the 7.9 ms worst-case tick when a long cold-cache path is solved.

~25% of path requests in a dense city still fail their node budget and fall back to a straight-line walk, so a citizen occasionally cuts visually through a building. Root cause is outside my folder: GridSystem.find_path's octile heuristic is weighted in tile steps while its g-cost is weighted in terrain cost (6+ per tile), so it under-estimates ~6:1 and behaves closer to Dijkstra than A*. If [P01] scales the heuristic by the minimum terrain cost, my node budgets can drop by roughly 6x and both the failures and the 7.9 ms peak go away.

No building in game/content/buildings/ carries the &"medical" tag, so the infirmary path (walk to care, 3.2x recovery, medic trade) is exercised only by the fallback: care capacity is currently derived from housing (beds/4, nursing at home). Nothing in the shipped content produces food without a rubble_sorter (scrap->grain) plus a field_kitchen (grain->ration), and no scenario builds one. HeatFlow rewritten around a dense per-network index (new HeatTopology: CSR adjacency + PackedArrays keyed by a local index handed out in ascending building-id order; new HeatRoute holding a routing solution). Replaced ~10 hashed lookups and 2 method calls per graph edge with array indexing. Determinism stopped depending on remembering to sort: iterating 0..n-1 IS sorted-id order, so every keys.sort() disappeared rather than being trusted. 24.4 -> 10.4 ms/tick.

The keys.sort() inside the progressive-filling round loop (heat_flow.gd:454 in the old file) removed: the active set only shrinks across rounds, so the sorted union of active paths is computed once per _fill instead of twelve times per tier per pass.

Residual reroutes given their own storage instead of clobbering the cross-tick routing cache. The old code set route_dirty on every in-tick reroute, so any network carrying a deficit re-ran a full BFS every tick - which is most of every night. Primary routes fell from 4386 to 765 over 2572 ticks.

Residual routes memoised by signature (route gates + tech + the saturated-tile set + the seed set). In a steady night the same trunk saturates in the same order every tick: 10,518 full breadth-first floods became 380, a 96% hit rate. route_residual 2.66 -> 0.10 ms/tick. 10.4 -> 7.9 ms/tick.

WarmthField.set_source fast path: it was formatting a String shape key and hashing it for every radiating building every tick, for a shape that only changes when research moves the radius.
One cached Array[HeatNode] in heat, shared by _burn_fuel / _thermal / _radiate / _pull_fuel / serialize, instead of three dictionary walks over every building each tick. 7.9 -> 6.5 ms/tick.

FlowField given a cell budget and resume(), plus a RAISE_LIMIT above which a repair gives up and re-floods instead (invalidating a shadow is the one phase that cannot be suspended safely - half an invalidation leaves stale-low integrations the following flood refuses to improve). A shadow buffer answers queries from the previous complete field while a budgeted re-flood is in flight, so pathing never blinks. Worst grid tick 69.5 -> 7.7 ms.

Godot 4.7 already optimises member access and `for d in range(8)` beats a hand-written while loop. A full flood is 435,000 edge relaxations at ~172 ns each - that is GDScript's floor, which is why the fix had to be budgeting rather than micro-optimisation.

what_is_fake: The build menu. `LcnBuildMenuBootstrap.install()` calls `tree.root.add_child(menu)` from inside boot's _ready; Godot refuses with 'Parent node is busy setting up children, add_child() failed' (build_menu_bootstrap.gd:56). install() sets _installed=true and returns the orphaned node anyway, so boot's null-check passes and it logs 'view installed: ... + build menu'. Across three clean launches the line `[ui.build_menu] installed: N panels` never appears, while `[hud] installed (7 panels)` and `[overlay] ready - 6 lenses` both do. _ready never ran. The palette search over 60 buildings, the tech tree, the law panel, the recipe browser and the blueprint library are all built and all outside the scene tree. The automation pillar. logistics.belt_lines = 0 and logistics.items_moved = 0 for all 24000 ticks of first_night, and not one of the five shipped scenarios (first_night, economy_60min, smoke, stress_1000, determinism) places a belt, inserter or splitter. The green gate. check.sh reports 45 suites / 768 tests / 15797 asserts / determinism sha256 IDENTICAL / PERF OK / CHECK GREEN, and the harness prints '0 error(s)'. result.what_is_real: The simulation is not a facade. Heat is a real network with grids, node counts, buffers, per-building freeze points and topology (the lens correctly reported 'GRID 2 0/11 u/s 1 node(s) NO SOURCE' and 'separate grids do not share heat'). Society is genuinely Frostpunk-shaped: factions with approval, grievances with named causes, demands carrying deadline ticks and written speeches, ultimatums, unrest stages 0-4 and despair stages. Threat telegraphs in four steps with approach directions and a heat-signature budget. Research is 45 nodes with pacing and a rate_reason string ('0 lab(s), 0 workshop(s), heat 55%, cold 100%'). The belt code is real - two independent lanes, sub-tile positions, undergrounds that pair within a span, splitters with output priority and filters - and its 39 unit tests test the right things (side-loading merges onto the near lane only, two belts nose to nose deliver nothing, a tunnel costs the time it saves). Determinism genuinely holds across two separate processes. And the legibility layer that scored 2 last round now exists and does real work: the bottleneck lens draws a line from every starving building back to the tile strangling it and labels the source 'SOURCE AT FULL OUTPUT -> 10 buildings draw on it'; the warmth lens draws labelled isotherms ('SURVIVAL LINE -10 C', 'COMFORT +10 C'); the freeze lens gives per-building countdowns ('freezes in 46s') and a verdict line. That is the largest single improvement in the build.
result.visual_verdict: Competent, coherent mood; no art direction. The palette holds together across dawn/dusk/night and the hearth glow with lit windows genuinely reads as warmth in a dead landscape. Cropped and upscaled, the Hearth is a stepped stone bowl with a fire in it and housing blocks are gabled roofs with lit windows - fine at 40px. Everything else is thin: the ground is featureless brown noise with no roads, no tile grid and no snow behaviour around buildings, so the terrain edge reads as a stain rather than a plain; large buildings are dark rectangles containing three miniature houses at a scale that contradicts the rectangle; heat pipes are one sprite repeated ten times so a mains run reads as railway track; citizens are 6px grey smudges. Then the overlay layer breaks the frame: the world overlay sits on CanvasLayer 70 and the HUD on 65, so in three of seven screenshots world labels are painted straight over the clock panel - forty 'building' badges smeared in a line across the top of assault.png, two 'FROZEN -25 C' plates over the nightfall countdown in deep_night.png. The hardcoded camera tour (PlayController.TOUR) also puts the city in the bottom third of the frame at t=7200 and t=8800 with two thirds of the screen empty snow, and the bottleneck lens fires red leader lines off the top edge to buildings that are not on screen.
result.biggest_gap: Nothing you built is reachable, and the gate cannot see it. The build menu is never in the scene tree - `tree.root.add_child(menu)` fails at build_menu_bootstrap.gd:56 on every launch, install() swallows it, and boot cheerfully logs 'view installed: ... + build menu'. So the palette, tech tree, law panel, recipe browser and blueprint library do not exist in the running game, the society system issues ultimatums demanding a law the player has no UI to sign, and the entire logistics pillar has no command path from a human at all. Meanwhile 768 tests, a determinism replay and a perf gate all report green, because Log.errors counts only the project's own logger and every engine-level error is invisible. Fix the boot seam (defer the add, and have install() return null unless menu.is_inside_tree() so the existing 'B will do nothing' warning actually fires), then make check.sh fail on engine errors so this class of break can never be green again. Until a human can open a menu, the eleven systems underneath are a simulation, not a game.

comparisons.why: I placed 19 belt tiles and 4 loading arms myself and then looked at the frame: the ground where they sit is empty dirt. Nothing in game/view calls belts_for_view() or items_for_view(), and logistics deliberately does not emit Bus.building_placed (logistics_system.gd:844-846), so belts, inserters and items are never handed to the renderer. Then I opened the one lens built for them, F5 LOGISTICS, and it threw every frame: 'Invalid access to property or key backed_up' at game/ui/overlays/logistics_lens.gd:66 — the lens reads b["backed_up"] but overlay_probe.gd:138-147 emits only cell/load/dir/stalled/tunnel. The screenshot run aborted at that shot. This was never caught because the reference scenario first_night contains zero belts (logistics.belt_lines = 0 for all 24000 ticks).
comparisons.what_they_do_that_we_dont: Factorio draws the recipe icon on every machine in alt-mode, so a screenshot of a base is self-documenting; it draws each item as its own sprite riding the belt at the belt's real speed, so you diagnose a bottleneck by watching where the gaps start; it tints underground pairs and shows their span; hovering a belt gives items/s. We draw nothing on machines about what they make, nothing on belts at all, and our belt lens crashes the moment a belt exists.

comparisons.why: 12 recipes, depth 5 (ore->plate->gear/coil->circuit/pipe->heat_core), which is a respectable skeleton. But the loop does not close: production._refill() (production_system.gd:821-847) pulls inputs only from ProdStore, which is a facade over the single global city ledger (prod_store.gd:38-45). The documented belt->machine entry point, production_system.gd:313 offer_input(), has zero callers anywhere in game/. I proved the consequence with my own layout: after 6000 ticks the belt and arms had physically delivered 196 iron_ore into smelter #24's store, and that same machine reported state 'missing_input: iron_ore' with 0 crafts. A machine works anywhere on the map if the city stock has the item, and a belt that reaches it changes nothing.
comparisons.what_they_do_that_we_dont: In Factorio inputs must physically arrive, which is the entire game: ratios (24 stone furnaces saturate a yellow belt), bus design, throughput math, fluids, modules and beacons, trains for distance. We have no ratio pressure at all because every machine is fed by teleport from a global ledger; belts are a parallel decorative system.

comparisons.why: The sim side is real: place_line drags an L-shaped run and auto-rotates each tile, place_area, remove_area, undo/redo with a depth metric, blueprint capture/paste/save/load, and a can_place() ghost validated every frame. But I launched the actual game and the build menu never installs: 'Parent node is busy setting up children, add_child() failed' at game/ui/build_menu/build_menu_bootstrap.gd:56 (from boot.gd:115). The 'installed: N panels, hotkeys B I T N L' line never appears. Worse, install() still returns the orphan node, so boot.gd:116's 'the build menu declined to install' warning never fires. What is left is PlayController's fallback 15-kind Q/E cycle (play_controller.gd:25-30) — which contains no belt, no inserter, no splitter and no smelter.
comparisons.what_they_do_that_we_dont: Factorio: pick anything from a searchable inventory, drag a belt and watch it turn corners under the cursor, shift-click to copy machine settings, blueprint books with absolute/relative snapping, ghost-place a whole factory and let bots build it, Ctrl+Z across arbitrary history. We ship a 15-item hotkey carousel because the palette that would replace it fails to enter the scene tree.

comparisons.why: Our clock is genuinely excellent and I watched it work: NIGHTFALL IN 0:42 in red at the top, 'WARNING 3/4 - First Frost in 1:30. The wind has stopped. It always stops first.', ambient falling -17 to -29C, per-building freeze countdowns rendered on the map ('freezes in 46s'), 'The Hearth grid is 42 heat short' with the cause and the fix on the next two lines, 26 buildings frozen solid by the end. The warmth lens draws an actual survival isoline at -10C and a comfort line at +10C around the city, which is more legible than anything Frostpunk shows. What is missing is consequence: over 24000 ticks with unrest at 86, despair stage 2 and an ultimatum issued, citizens.dead_total was 0 and population still grew 18 -> 47. The dread is on the meters, never in the ground.
comparisons.what_they_do_that_we_dont: Frostpunk makes the cold take things you cannot get back: people freeze and die by name, the sick fill the medical posts, buildings you rely on go dark permanently, and the storm's temperature drop physically consumes the map from the edges inward. Our worst night costs five structures and nobody at all.

comparisons.why: The system underneath is the real thing and I drove it: signing Child Labour produced 'proposed Child Labour, 4.0 hours of argument' -> 'law in force' -> the Hearthside faction opening a grievance that quotes the law back at you ('You have our children. We would like to know what you are doing with them.') -> a named demand ('You will not put them in the pits. Say it now, in front of everyone') -> 'demand failed: The Hearthside asked you to hold off, and you signed anyway' -> unrest stages 1/2/3 -> an ultimatum. 31 laws with argument_for/argument_against/signed_line, faction approval deltas, exclusion pairs and a seal cooldown. And none of it is reachable: the only command that signs a law is built in game/ui/build_menu/law_model.gd:467, inside the build menu that fails to install, so in the game I launched a player cannot sign anything.
comparisons.what_they_do_that_we_dont: Frostpunk stages the decision: the law tree on screen, the signing animation on the book, named faction leaders arguing before and after, and an epilogue that reads your choices back and judges them. We have better sim plumbing for consequence than we have any way to present a choice — there is no decision surface at all.

comparisons.why: Read across opening/build/midday/dusk/deep_night/dawn, the day cycle grade is real and the hearth is the best thing in the build — a fire bowl with warm bloom and lit windows anchoring the city. But zoomed in on dusk: no snow accumulates on any roof, no chimney smoke, no crowd (24 agents render as tiny props you have to hunt for), no wind in the city, and the three housing blocks are pixel-identical. At default zoom 50-60% of the 1920x1080 frame is a flat marbled cloud texture that reads as fog, not as a frozen plain. The deep_night frame is mostly unreadable dark smudges.
comparisons.what_they_do_that_we_dont: Frostpunk: volumetric snowfall that settles and drifts, ice creeping across the lens, crowds physically massing around the generator, chimney smoke bending in the wind, the generator rising as a structure you built, and a colour grade that goes bone-blue as the temperature drops. We change the palette and the light energy; we do not change the world's state of matter.

comparisons.why: Our panels, where they load, are better written than either reference: 'Scrap runs out in 50 seconds / 960 left, falling by 1.1k a minute / -> Mine more, make more, or stop spending it', the heat header reading '114 / 175 heat/s  -42 short', and each lens carrying a one-line self-explanation ('one hue per grid - if two halves differ, they are not connected'). Against that, three things I hit myself: the build menu does not exist in a real session; game/ui/hud/vitals_widget.gd:78 throws 'String formatting error: not all arguments converted' on every HUD repaint (the % operator binds to the last concatenated fragment, which has no %s), spamming the console continuously; and in the ALT-detail assault frame ~30 identical circular 'building' badges pile into an unreadable smear straight across the clock panel, while bottleneck leader lines shoot off the top of the screen to buildings outside the viewport.
comparisons.what_they_do_that_we_dont: Factorio's UI is unglamorous but it never fails to open, never collides its own labels, and gives you a real entity inspection panel with contents, recipe, modules and status on every click. Frostpunk gives every panel a diegetic frame and a signing ritual. We have the best sentences and the least reliable surface.

comparisons.why: The in-world coaching is genuinely first-rate and it is all live-state-driven, not canned: research auto-starts with a reason quoting current numbers ('Belt Drives - You are walking ore across your own base... 6 machines, drills and stores to keep fed'), stalls honestly ('Watchfires stalled at 49% - needs 13 coal'), the attention panel names the cause and the fix, the F1-F6 lens list is permanently on screen with 'ALT details' next to it, and every lens explains itself. That beats Factorio's in-game teaching outright. It cancels out because the surfaces where teaching would continue — the palette with tooltips, the recipe browser, the 45-node tech tree, the Book of Laws — are all inside the menu that does not install, and the fallback Q/E palette is never announced anywhere on screen.
comparisons.what_they_do_that_we_dont: Both references guarantee a first-run path: Factorio's tutorial campaign hand-places your first drill-to-furnace, and its tech tree is always one key away; Frostpunk gates the first hour behind sequenced prompts. A player launching our build gets a world, no menu, and no statement that Q and E cycle a hidden palette.

comparisons.why: What actually moves in my frames: the nightfall clock, meter bars, alert cards appearing, and freeze countdowns. What does not move: items (invisible), belts (invisible), enemies (the frame literally named 'assault' has combat.enemies_alive = 0 — wave 1 was 6 kills and already over), and machines (5 machines in a 243-building city, active_machines oscillating 0-1, 78 crafts in 24000 ticks). The best minute in this build is a heat crisis at deep night, and it is a good minute — but it is a minute of reading text, not of watching a system run.
comparisons.what_they_do_that_we_dont: Factorio's baseline pleasure is watching your own machine work: items streaming, inserters swinging, furnaces flashing, and the audio ticking along with it. Every one of those channels is either unrendered or idle here.

result.single_biggest_gap: The automation loop does not close: belts and inserters are simulated but are neither drawn nor connected to production. Three specific holes, one pillar. (1) production_system.gd:313 offer_input() — the documented belt->machine input path — has zero callers, and _refill() pulls only from the global city ledger (prod_store.gd:38), so a smelter sat at 'missing_input: iron_ore' with 196 iron_ore that my belt had physically delivered into it. (2) Nothing in game/view calls belts_for_view()/items_for_view(), so 19 belts and 4 loading arms rendered as bare dirt. (3) The F5 logistics lens dies on b['backed_up'] (logistics_lens.gd:66, key not emitted by overlay_probe.gd:138) the instant a belt exists. Fixing these makes the belt a real input path, puts items on screen, and un-breaks the one lens for them — moving automation_readability, factory_depth, base_building_feel, ui_craft and moment_to_moment_feel together. Nothing else on this list moves five dimensions.
result.would_a_factorio_player_keep_playing: No, not past the first twenty minutes. They would press B for a build menu and get nothing (it fails add_child() at boot, build_menu_bootstrap.gd:56), discover the fallback Q/E palette by accident and find it has no belt in it, then — if they got a belt down through some other route, as I did by scripting it — watch it deliver 196 ore into a smelter that keeps reporting 'missing_input', with the belt itself invisible and its diagnostic overlay throwing a script error. What would hold them for that first twenty minutes is real and worth protecting: the nightfall clock, the heat-grid deficit readout, the per-building freeze timers, the bottleneck lens saying 'SOURCE AT FULL OUTPUT -> 10 buildings draw on it', and research lines that quote your own base back at you. That is a genuinely good survival-legibility game. It is not yet an automation game, and a Factorio player will work that out on the first belt.
